intent: Test the mass lever. Keep the validated iteration-6 design (track 0.10 m, body 0.10 x 0.12 m, sensor array x = -0.08 to 0.08 at 0.04 m spacing, 0.016 m footprint, y 0.05) and reduce mass from 0.6 to 0.5 kg. Target: s-bend and slalom progress above 0.2 and max_error near or below 0.06 m, with the oval finish rate at or above 55% and steering_oscillation below 0.25.
learning: Hypotheses: (1) Mass is a real turn-response lever. Lighter mass at the same geometry raises s-bend and slalom progress above 0.2, with max_error near 0.06 m. (2) Oval steering_oscillation rises with the lighter mass but stays below 0.25. If it does not, the next step is a lower sensor lead (y 0.03). (3) If s-bend and slalom progress does not change from iteration 6 (0.181 and 0.191), mass is not the limit and the next lever is sensor lead or the controller-side geometry. Please report per-track values for progress, max_error and steering_oscillation on the s-bend and slalom, and the oval finish rate.
rationale: Iteration 6 (wheel_track 0.10, body 0.10 x 0.12, mass 0.6, sensor array x = -0.08 to 0.08 at 0.04 m spacing, 0.016 m footprint, y 0.05) is the best design so far at 289.8. Its oval finish rate is 65%, with zero line loss on the oval and 0.1 events per run, and oval steering_oscillation is 0.216, under the 0.25 threshold. The s-bend and slalom improved clearly over iteration 4: progress rose from 0.127 to 0.181 on the s-bend and from 0.093 to 0.191 on the slalom. Both still end off_track at max_error about 0.062 to 0.065, which is at or just above the 0.06 m floor. The Integrator's feedback sets a conditional rule: if s-bend or slalom progress rises above 0.13 while max_error stays near 0.06 m, the body and mass lever is working, so the next step is mass 0.5 kg with track 0.10 m and body_length 0.10 m fixed. Iteration 6 meets that condition (0.181 and 0.191 progress, max_error about 0.06). The narrower track and the 0.12 m body were both ruled out by the oval results, so I keep track 0.10 m and body_length 0.10 m. Sensing is unchanged because line loss is near zero, and sensor y stays at 0.05 because oval oscillation is below 0.25. I am reducing mass only, so the race isolates the mass effect. Expected result: s-bend and slalom progress rise above 0.2 with max_error still near 0.06 m, and the oval finish rate holds at or above 55%. Risk: a lighter robot may raise oval steering_oscillation or overshoot, which the oval race will show.
